## 1. S1 to S6

**S1: right, in both cases you ask about.**
- Parity: a birth with a fresh distinction adds a row with a column of its own, and an IMPLIED birth adds a row already in the span. Every old state extends whether or not any knot passes.
- Several births taking the same shared distinction change nothing: each closes on its own fresh distinction.
- Not-all-equal: the same, since a fresh distinction can always be set unequal to an input.
- Say what it excludes: LITERAL, FLOOR0, ONE-FEWER, and anything compared across B(ii), because removal changes the allowed states.

**S2: true, but not tight, and "any start" is wrong.**
- Exact statement: a fresh f of u is tied to something exactly when u has one fresh distinction and its inputs are all tied equal before its round. f is then tied unequal to each input.
- By induction, from a start with no tie, no made distinction is ever tied, whether or not knots pass. The "every knot passes" hypothesis can go.
- A failing knot (inputs constrained together but not all forced equal) ties nothing. So "the exceptions are exactly … failing knots" is too broad.
- Later and earlier distinctions are both covered: the flip argument gives two allowed states differing only in f.
- A same-round birth sharing an input is harmless: only u holds f.
- Counterexample to "any start": Fano less one knot ties a = b = c. Add start knots {l, a, b} and {x, b, c}; then l = x in every state. Their join takes l and x, receives one fresh f, and f is tied to l.
- The registered starts have at most two holders, so S6 makes them tie-free. P3 is then a true check with no knot-test condition.

**S3: right, with four precisions.**
- "Sum to a rule" should read "the sum over the field of two elements lies in the span of the rules before the round", zero included.
- If v is itself an input, the other inputs sum to a rule and the maker fails the knot test. So a passing maker of a distinction tied to v never holds v.
- The same-round clause holds only when v's maker also has exactly one fresh distinction; with two or more, never.
- "Two or more fresh hands nothing on" relies on IMPLIED; without it the two could be tied to each other.
- The same-round clause is never needed for the values sense: v exists after round s and the tied distinction is made later.

**S4: right in every case you list; I found no counterexample.**
- Shorter proof: an offshoot's parent q holds exactly one place of its own parent g, namely d. Its take is by rule not held by g, and a join's other inputs were loose elsewhere.
- If g is not a start knot, the distinction g took from its own parent is shared, not held by q, and so eligible. This needs neither RELEASE nor anything about barred distinctions.
- If g is a start knot, g acted in the round it made q and (RELEASE) spent every other loose place.
- CANCEL-WAIT: g made q, so it was not waiting. CANCEL-RETIRE and B(i): a knot holding barred distinctions was a member, so it has no children.
- Joins, including joins of start knots and of a start knot's offshoot with a later knot, have two or more inputs and receive one. The exception class is therefore narrower than drafted: only offshoots of start knots.
- STEPS-1 with several parents: any one parent supplies a candidate, so the union is not empty.
- It also holds under HOLD: a start knot that keeps something was in a group, so it has a shared place.
- STEPS-2: it holds from one generation later. An offshoot of q takes whenever q has a grandparent; the candidate is what q's parent took from that grandparent. Two fresh distinctions go only to offshoots of start knots and of knots whose parents are all start knots. This matches the prototype's round-2 copies.
- State the consequence by maker, not by round. Under CANCEL-WAIT a start knot may act late.
- With s = 0 and STEPS-1, round-1 offshoots of start knots do not take and hold two. So S4 alone does not close form or build on the beside designs; that part is a check.
- FLOOR1 never gives more than two fresh distinctions, so a member holding three is never made under any taking rule.

**S5, S6: right.** No registered law uses them; they are record checks only.

**S7:** "a passing knot has no two of its own places tied" is false for a two-place IMPLIED knot. Add "with three or more places".

## 2. The claim

- **C is the right claim for values under parity, but not as worded.**
  - It quantifies over the four choice rules after the fact. That fits the law to the pattern; fix one rule first, or state C four times.
  - It says "one made X", but in the six beside designs X is a start pattern. For a made X the class has two real members (made-3, made-4). Split C by whether X is made.
  - The drafter has seen it fail. Register it as predicted to fail, not as "reported".
- **The first "cannot hold" is not honest as worded.**
  - It is a fact about what FLOOR1 with the fresh count by distinct inputs can make: a take costs the birth its second fresh distinction. It is not a fact about copying.
  - The class 𝒴 (members holding two or three) lies outside what that ration makes after the first offshoots, so the negative is by choice of class.
  - Honest wording: "under this ration every knot made after the start's own offshoots holds one loose distinction, so no part with a member holding two is made at all, copied or not."
- **The second is honest for "tied" only**, from a tie-free start (item 1 and item 4).
- **Check the pairing of the law.** The fold result's P11, as quoted in its head, gives the cheapest laws as STEPS-1 under FLOOR1 and MET under the cap of three. The draft's primary is MET with FLOOR1, which is neither. MET with CAP-3 is the fold study's own cheapest pairing, and S4 fails there.
- **Yes, form should be an arm of its own**, under MET with CAP-3(t) and under fresh by parents, with its own prediction. As drafted, the swaps of run 5 are applied only to positive cases, so they never run on the form negatives.
- **The least the form arm must run for a negative to mean something:**
  - a reader control: the reading finds the two-knot part's own copies with no taking rule, and finds a planted copy;
  - a census showing the arm's law makes at least one part the same as each class member after round s; drop class members it cannot make;
  - at least two second patterns that are not the same, with the same X, rule and numbering;
  - B(i), B_X, the replacement run, and item 3's check;
  - the share of cases in which X's course differs with Y at all. If it never does, the negative means only "they did not meet".

## 3. The necessary condition

- **Not right as stated; right with two additions.**
  - A specificity clause: with Y′ in place of Y there are fewer than two of Y. The claim's section 4.2 has it ("of Y′, not of Y"); definitions 5.1 dropped it. Without it, an X that always makes two of everything passes with one course.
  - The copies must descend from X only. A copy from a birth with a parent in each can take its dependence through the Y parent, and the trace excludes such births.
- The trace's met sets are cut down to X's descendants, so read the mark on the roster's parts by origin as well as on the trace.
- It does not hold for values: the same takes up to renaming can be tied to different things.
- FD's fourth mark is defined by changing the holdings of the start knot Y descends from. Redefine it here on the replacement runs.
- Register it as a check (any form or build positive made by X's descendants only must show the mark) and as a reported reading on every replacement pair.
- To the owner, state it as a necessary condition not yet seen (16 pairs). It is not a reason.

## 4. Not-all-equal and "values"

- **(a) is required.** Your count is right: 4 of 6. Reword to "no made distinction is ever tied to another". The plain sentence overstates.
- **(b): leave it out; state it as a limit and a direction.** Reasons:
  - The uniform weighting over allowed states does not survive growth. Adding NAE(a, b, f) moves the share of a = b from 1/2 to 1/3, so S1 fails for shares and every number depends on the round read.
  - A second natural weighting (old states uniform, then fresh uniform) gives 3/4 where the first gives 2/3. The reading is of the weighting.
  - A share is not "the same value"; it would be a fourth sense the owner did not ask for.
  - Only the made designs through about round 3 are small enough to count.
- **If you register it anyway:**
  - Method: exact count by enumeration, halved by the flip symmetry.
  - Bound: 26 distinctions; above that, "not counted".
  - Cross-check: a model counter on the small cases.
  - No prediction; name the weighting and the round.
- **Under parity it means nothing new.** Each share is 1 (tied) or 1/2. A share of 0 cannot occur, because the all-zero state is allowed.

## 5. The paired test for values

- **"Fewer than two with Y barred" is not a sound test of input.**
  - A tie to a free v that is tied to nothing of X is already a dependence on Y's value. Barring Y removes Y's births, not its values.
  - It would reject the cleanest copier: X copying a value of a Y that does nothing.
  - Per place it is confounded by naming: in P6's case barring Y shifts the place from 16 to 10 because the names move.
- Report B(i) as "needs Y's births or not", counted over any place of Y by tie class. Do not make it a condition.
- **The right tests:**
  - at least one of the two descends from X (the origin, already there);
  - the replacement run;
  - renaming the start, which is the test that the choice is not the numbering's;
  - B_X, for Y handing on its own value.
- **B(ii) is not needed for values**: it removes v. It is also undefined on every beside design, since Y's members are start knots.
- Add "v is tied to no place of X after round s", not only "not a place of X".
- **Loose at the round read**, and usable, with both at the same round. "Loose at its birth" is true of every fresh distinction, so it would count a chain as two.
- Note that under RELEASE with offshoots the two must be made in the same round. Report whether both are later taken by different births (the note's "two users").

## 6. Definitions

- **"X meets Y"** is undefined for patterns, and C uses it. Define the meeting round (FD 4.3, one part) and say whether ties before it count.
- **Y's build.** "The knots of Y's members" should read "Y's members and every knot a member meets".
  - The search is feasible to 500 knots: the pattern has at most about 8 knots; backtrack on knot signatures (places, loose, barred, holders).
  - Bound it: stop at two disjoint copies, or at 10,000 distinct knot sets and report "bound hit".
  - Say whether "disjoint" means no common knot or also no common place.
  - Run G's brute force for build copies has no round s on drawn structures. Specify the pattern and the candidates.
- **Two of it in form.** "Holding a member" should be "containing". Say how a part with members of both origins is counted, and "at some round" against "at the last round".
- **Origins.** A knot descending from both through different parents is "from both"; that is consistent.
  - "Of X" includes births with a third part's knot as a parent; say so.
  - "Made by X": say whether a birth from both counts (the claim's section 4.4 says yes; C does not say), and whether both of the two or at least one.
- **B_X** is fine.
- **The replaced second pattern.**
  - It is undefined for the pairs of run 3, so C is testable on run 2 only.
  - "The rest unchanged" is false on the beside designs: the dead knot z changes with Y.
  - Say which place of Y′ answers to v: any, by tie class.
- **"The same stated choice rule."**
  - All four rules read names. BY-COUNT indexes the eligible list "from the oldest", so it does not use "the structure only".
  - Replacing Y renumbers the start: e is 17 with three-222 and 12 with one-2.
  - Define it as the same rule text on the registered naming convention, and make the naming part of what is supplied.
  - Require that a positive "under a stated rule" survive every registered renaming.
- **Every choice.**
  - The number of histories is not known before enumerating: count depth-first and stop at 60,001.
  - For drawing, fix the order of calls (birth order), the call itself (`randrange` over candidates sorted by name), whether a single candidate consumes a call, and the exact design and law strings.
  - The seed for the 3,000 is missing from the Runs table.
  - Run G's generator of drawn structures is unspecified.
- **The five shares.**
  - They are counts, not shares.
  - "Bearer" is defined only for places of Y, yet three columns use places of X or of neither.
  - Say what "of neither" covers (e? made distinctions?), whether "made by X" means both, and the round.
- **The set V** is used by no run. Drop it.
- **"The smallest pattern it fails on"** needs an order (members, then places).
- **The knot-test filter** is fine. Also report cases from runs with a failing knot, marked.

## 7. Predictions

- **True by construction:** P1, by S4 (exclude fresh by parents and B(ii) in its wording); P3, by the stronger S2; P10's parity clause, since an offshoot has at most two inputs and a verdict is fixed at birth; P4 and P5 under COPY-LAW, apart from the start-offshoot check.
- **P0 is nearly empty.** The engine imports the fold engine, so equality cannot fail; and the "independent" engine shares the growth code with the prototype. Say so.
- **Replications of the prototype only:** P2 (the CAP-3 and Q runs, and "at most 3 of 180"), P4 and P5 under CAP-3 and STEPS-2, P6, P7, P8, P9, P10's not-all-equal clause.
- **Not decidable by the registered runs:** P4's second clause and P5's "under any swap", because run 5 swaps positive cases only; C for a made X beyond two patterns; the "why" of step 4.
- **Expected to fail on an independent engine:**
  - P8, by sampling. Rates are near 1 in 3,000 to 1 in 10,000 against 20,000 draws, so a design can miss or two-33 can hit. Register the eight histories as take lists to replay, and leave two-33 open.
  - P6 and P7, on any difference in reading: the round read, usable, a birth from both.
  - P2's exact "3".
  - P9 should hold.
- **P6 and P7 are over-specified.**
  - State P6 by structure: the design, the law, two loose distinctions made by X's descendants tied to a place of Y's member that a join of Y took.
  - Keep the names in a replay listing, not as a failure condition.
  - Split P7 into "survives 2", "vanishes under every other choice", "vanishes under renaming", and the rest reported.
- **P11 should be (a): predicted to fail.**
- **Missing:**
  - a check for step 2 (the record checks are not registered);
  - a run with Y never there, on a start without Y and z, which is the plain "without the second pattern";
  - the birth-by-birth reason for the smallest failing pattern;
  - a statement that, for parity, the expected result reaches neither arm of the owner's stop.

## 8. Supplied or made

- **The five verdicts are not mutually exclusive.** "Supplied by the start" is "reported alongside", and B_X having two does not exclude X making two.
- They mix three questions. Give each its own exclusive answer:
  - who made the two: X's descendants, Y's, both, neither;
  - what fixed the takes: a rule that survives renaming, a rule that does not, a history picked;
  - where X and the linking knot come from: the start or the growth.
- "Made" is earned only when all three are the growth's. All three are decidable from registered runs once renaming is run on every positive.
- **The disclosed case in one sentence:** supplied: a start pattern, joined to the second pattern through a start distinction, under a rule that picks by the start's numbering, comes to hold one value of one second pattern at two loose places, and it is gone when the start is renamed or the second pattern changed; only the births that carry the value are made.

## 9. Scope and honesty

- **A positive for C would show** one bit of each registered second pattern at two loose places, under parity, one rule and one numbering.
- **It would not show** two of the pattern, two users, a class beyond the seven distinct registered forms, a made X on the beside designs, or anything under not-all-equal.
- **The expected result shows** what this ration can make, that not-all-equal growth from a tie-free start ties nothing, and that parity ties are cheap and follow the choice.
- **It does not show** that no made pattern can copy under parity, anything about form where S4 fails, dependence under a weighting, or anything past the bounds.
- **The plain sentence as I would write it:** "Under the law we fixed, the ration gives every later knot one loose distinction, so the part that copied itself stops and no part of that kind is made again; that is the ration's doing and says nothing yet about copying a form. Under not-all-equal no made distinction is ever tied to another. Under parity a value of a second pattern can reach two loose places, but in every case found the choice we supplied put it there: it happens under one rule, for one pattern, numbered one way. We have neither a copier nor a reason there cannot be one."
- **Sentences that blur law and pattern:**
  - C's "one stated choice rule (OLDEST, NEWEST, IN-TURN or BY-COUNT) such that": the rule is picked for the pattern.
  - F1's "the choice then plays the owner's index": that is copying placed in the law. Keep it labelled as a control.
  - The name COPY-LAW in a study whose premise is that copying is not a law. Gloss it at each first use.
  - "The base law under which the two-knot part copies itself", used of a law under which it does not.
  - "Aimed at" and "points X at Y": write "more often, under the named weighting".

## 10. Words

- **the first pattern, the second pattern:** keep.
- **two of it in form:** no term. Write "two parts the same as Y"; keep "form" in the owner's quoted words only.
- **build:** drop the noun; it reads as "what Y builds", and includes knots Y did not make. Write "Y's knots" (its members and every knot a member meets).
- **a copy of a build:** "a renaming of Y's knots among the made knots".
- **bearer:** no new word; "bears" already means "gives birth to" in the record. Write "a made distinction tied to v" and "two loose made distinctions tied to v". Drop "bears" from section 0.
- **two of it in values:** "two usable loose made distinctions tied to one place of Y".
- **copier:** keep for the owner's sense only; add the glossary line re-reading the record's heading.
- **of X / of Y / joint:** "of Y" already means "held by Y" for places. Write "descended from X only / from Y only / from both / from neither". Keep "joint birth" in FD's sense only.
- **the drawing weighting:** "the take-by-take weighting".
- **history:** keep; the fold result uses it so. Define once: one run with every take fixed.
- **hand on:** keep, defined through "tied".
- **the second pattern copying itself after a meeting:** "the second pattern handing on its own value" for values (the draft's own phrase); for form, the shared definitions' "returns".
- Also change "beside" and "hung on", which are words of place: "present with X from round 0", "met by a dead knot".

## 11. The eight open questions

1. Keep C for values, fixed as in item 2 and predicted to fail. Add form as its own arm under MET with CAP-3 and under fresh by parents; add it, do not substitute it.
2. Yes, in every case named, and under HOLD. The exception is offshoots of start knots only. Under STEPS-2 it holds from one generation later.
3. Not tight. A failing knot's fresh distinction is tied only when its inputs are all tied equal, which cannot arise from a tie-free start. CARRY's failing join ties nothing unless that holds.
4. The tie is the input. The replacement and renaming runs are the tests. B(i) is reported, not required. B(ii) does not apply to values.
5. Usable and loose, both at the round read. Report chains apart, and whether both are later taken.
6. Fair if labelled, but X is then supplied by the start: a separate arm, outside the made-X claim. Make STEPS-2 primary for the came-apart arm, with its cost stated.
7. Register F1 as a control with replayable histories ("the knot law allows it; the choice decides it"). It is not a fallback that could earn "copier".
8. Item 10.

## 12. Verdict

**Freeze after listed changes.**

Required, in order of importance:
1. Reconcile the primary law with the fold result's P11. Register MET with CAP-3(t) and fresh by parents as a form and build arm with its own class, controls and prediction.
2. Reword both "cannot hold" statements (the ration and by maker; "tied", tie-free start, no knot-test condition) and the plain sentence.
3. Values test: drop "fewer than two with Y barred" as a condition, count by tie class, add "tied to nothing of X", usable and loose at one round, and require renaming for "under a stated rule".
4. C: fix the rule beforehand, split made X from start X, predict failure.
5. Item 3's check, with the specificity clause restored in definitions 5.1 and the fourth mark redefined on replacement runs.
6. Predictions: remove the undecidable clauses of P4 and P5; state P6 and P7 by structure and split them; give P8 replayable histories; separate P2's CAP-3 part.
7. Definitions: the meeting round, origins, "made by X", the table's columns, the enumeration and drawing procedure, replacement on the beside designs, run G's brute force.
8. Verdicts as three questions.
9. Words: bearer, build, of X / of Y, the F4 name.
10. Say that the engine shares the fold engine's growth code, and what P0 therefore does not test.

Optional:
- the not-all-equal share as a stated direction;
- S4 extended to STEPS-2 and HOLD;
- the "two users" reading;
- a run with Y never there;
- dropping the set V;
- the fix to S7;
- a registered check of the record (step 2).
